sources: Paradox Nemesis and free 3.0 espionage announcements; verify selected 4.5.2 rules in game
steps: Open Contacts and select the empire you want to investigate.
Open its Espionage view. If Establish Spy Network is offered, assign an envoy there.
Watch the intel and infiltration shown in game before choosing an operation; operation choices may depend on DLC and other conditions.
check: Check the target empire's Espionage screen for the action and its requirements.

sources: Official 4.5 Cygnus Pop Group notes; growth drivers need selected-version in-game validation
steps: Open the colony's Population view and inspect growth, assembly and migration progress.
Check the relevant tooltips and the colony's housing, habitability and open jobs before changing a building or policy.
check: The save parser does not yet verify this colony's growth rate, assembly, migration or available growth actions.

sources: Selected policy fields in save; eligibility must be checked in the installed 4.5.2 rules and game UI
steps: First decide whether you mean an empire-wide Policy or a change on this colony.
For a colony, inspect its designation, Decisions and job settings; for an empire Policy, open the Policies screen.
Check the listed effects and eligibility in game before changing anything.
check: The Guide reads selected policies, but cannot prove an alternative policy or planetary decision is available.

sources: Selected-save colony produces, upkeep and jobs; local in-game totals need reconciliation
steps: Compare this colony's production and upkeep with the resource your empire needs most.
Inspect open and disabled jobs before adding another district or building.
check: The saved colony figures may omit modifiers or not match every number shown in the game UI.

sources: Steam Guide 3829341385 (RedEye, 4.5.2) & GamerOfPassion 4.6 Beginner Guide — verify caps and fees in game
steps: Keep monthly Trade and Consumer Goods positive: running out of Trade cuts Job Efficiency by 25%, and a Consumer Goods shortage halves Research and Unity from jobs.

Local colony deficits cost Trade upkeep empire-wide; keep early colonies mixed until Trade surplus supports full specialization, and park idle fleets at Crew Quarters starbases to save Trade logistics upkeep.
Treat Market purchases as a short-term bridge (30% base Market fee) and watch storage caps (15,000 material, 50,000 Trade, 1,000 Influence) so surplus is not wasted.
check: Confirm your current Market fee, storage caps, and local colony deficits in the in-game Economy and Market screens.

sources: Official Stellaris 4.5.0/4.5.2 Cygnus notes and Nomads DLC documentation
steps: Manage onboard colonies, Governors, and Captains directly on your Arkships rather than looking for fixed planets.
Survey systems and place Waystations to connect Waylines and sustain Operational Reserves; defend exposed Waystations from fauna and raiders.
Check Weapon Preferences (Arkships) and Defense Preferences (Waystations) in Policies instead of settled starbase policies.
check: Confirm Arkship slots, Wayline connectivity, and active Nomad policies in game.

sources: Stellaris Wiki Ideology & Patch 4.6 (verified 4.6.0) — confirm exact save fields in game
steps: Creating, adopting (via a Fanatic Faction), or abandoning an Ideology costs 100 Influence + 1,000 Unity, with 0.75 Influence/month upkeep (abandoning adds -5 Stability and a 10-year lock).
Build Ideological Strength (0-1,000): 250 unlocks Galactic Halls tech, 500 unlocks Ideological Projection, 750 unlocks Absolute Ethic, and 1,000 unlocks Ideological Leverage.
Watch foreign-ideology pops: 30% foreign-ideology pops convert a Planetary Revolt into an Ideological Revolt, and Momentum events check every 10 years once >=25% follow an adopted ideology.
For Gestalt empires (Instincts / Directives), adopt via a 2,000 Society project or agenda after encountering an ideology.
check: Confirm Ideologies are enabled in galaxy settings and verify Strength, Momentum, Tenets, and Influence upkeep in game.

sources: Stellaris Wiki Crisis (4.5/4.6), Steam Guide 3843091177, and GamerOfPassion 4.6 Crisis Guide — verify loadouts in game
steps: Default Endgame Crisis first roll is 2450 (2425 with Jump Drives, no Fallen Empires, War in Heaven finished, or crisis resolution; 2400 only via Ultima Vigilis or both resolutions).
Stack crisis damage bonuses when threatened: Defender of the Galaxy (+50%), Galactic Threats Committee (+20%), and federation bonuses.
Refit fleets to counter the active crisis via Fleet -> Design Finder Crisis presets, and swap off Sapient Combat Computers if fighting the Contingency.
For Nomadic empires, crisis fleets destroy Arkships outright rather than disabling them.
check: Check your Mid-Game / End-Game year settings, Crisis Strength, and active Situation Log before committing fleets.

steps: Keep starting minister seats filled: leaving Minister of Defense, Head of Research, or Minister of State empty imposes -25% Naval Cap, Research Speed, or Diplomatic Weight.
Unlock 2 extra council seats via the Expand The Council agenda (in 4.6+, the 5th Council seat requires Galactic Administration tech rather than a 3rd civic).
Agenda cost is 7,000 progress (+0.1% per Empire Size above 100), scaled by Council Legitimacy; launch effects last 10 years with a 30-year cooldown and can be rushed with Unity.
check: Inspect your Council seats, Legitimacy, and Agenda progress in the Government -> Council screen.

steps: Default Leader Capacity is 3 per class: exceeding it multiplies upkeep by count/cap and cuts XP gain by 0.85^(leaders over cap) (Legendary Paragons and Eager leaders below level 4 are exempt).

Match Scientist veteran classes to roles: Statisticians on Council (+15% speed / +25% tech weight via Expertise), Analysts governing research worlds (+10%), Scholars for anomalies/digs, Explorers for surveying.
Leader ethics add pop ethic attraction (+10% on Council, +25% Sector, +50% governed Planet); in 4.6, rulers assigned to non-council posts also earn post XP.
check: Check each leader class cap, upkeep multiplier, and veteran trait options in the Leaders screen.

sources: Stellaris Wiki Subject empire & GamerOfPassion 4.6 Vassals Guide (verified 4.6.0)
steps: Watch Subject Loyalty (-100 to +100): below 0 turns Disloyal and blocks agreements; Pledge of Loyalty adds +1.5/month (+2.5/month at >=150 opinion), while multiple subjects trigger Divided Patronage drag.
Resource taxes adjust in 15% increments and block normal diplomatic trading of any taxed resource; subjects take -50% Diplomatic Weight (except Satrapies).
Do not place full system claims on a target if you want the Vassalize Casus Belli (full claims can disable it); Scholarium is typically the strongest Overlord specialist for research.
check: Verify subject agreement terms, Loyalty trend, Casus Belli eligibility, and Overlord holdings in game.

sources: Stellaris Wiki Megastructures & Deep space citadel (verified 4.6.0)
steps: Base concurrent multi-stage megastructure build limit is 1; clear anomalies on the target body first, and note that repaired ruined or conquered megastructures do not count against build caps.

Dyson Swarms scale by stage on star deposits (base cap 3, rising up to 5 with Mega-Engineering/Galactic Wonders); Deep Space Citadels (BioGenesis) cap at 1/system and hold up to 4 buildings like Crew Quarters (-25% docked upkeep).
Nomadic empires cannot build Habitats, Deep Space Citadels, Orbital Rings, or most multi-stage megastructures (only Quantum Catapult, Arc Furnace, and Ambition megastructures).
check: Confirm unlocked technologies, DLC eligibility, alloy/unity costs, and build cap in the Construction Ship menu.

steps: Reforming government has a 20-year cooldown and costs 10 Unity per point of Empire Size (Democratic 10-year elections reset policy and reform cooldowns on ruler change).

Account for authority trade-offs: Corporate increases Empire Size from colonies (and in 4.6+ allows Fanatic Authoritarian/Egalitarian); Hive Mind gives -25% Empire Size Effect; Machine gives +1 Nexus District on colonize.
In 4.6+, colony ascension Empire Size reduction caps at -90%, and Suppress/Promote Faction costs 1,000 Unity with a 15-25 year respawn lock if destroyed.
check: Confirm reform Unity cost, cooldown, and civic/ethic eligibility in the Government screen before reforming.

steps: Colony Stability below 25% risks a Planetary Revolt: first prioritize Entertainer or Maintenance Drone jobs (or build a Holo-Theatre) to fix negative Amenities.
Check Crime and fill Enforcer / Hunter-Seeker jobs (or use Anti-Crime Campaign / Precinct House), and confirm Housing and Living Standards are not crushing pop happiness.
For an active revolt Situation, inspect Planetary Decisions (Distribute Luxury Goods or Declare Martial Law / Compliance Protocols) and land assault armies or move pops to stabilize quickly.
In 4.6 Willpower campaigns, check whether >=30% foreign-ideology pops are turning the uprising into an Ideological Revolt.
check: Open the unstable colony's Stability tooltip and Situation Log in game immediately to see the exact happiness/crime drivers.

sources: GamerOfPassion 4.6 Automation Building Guide & r/Stellaris 4.x planetary automation notes
steps: Planetary Automation looks idle because it waits for available pops and builds one item at a time to avoid empty-district upkeep; use it for basic worlds and crime/enforcer slots (avoid on your Capital).

Automation Buildings (25%, Assembly Patterns) and Optimization Buildings (50%, Construction Templates) automate matching basic jobs planet-wide (1 per basic resource type, placed in matching resource zones).
Upkeep is 8 Energy (25%) or 10 Energy (50%) plus 4 Energy per 100 automated jobs (Technician break-even ~1,600/1,000 jobs base, ~640/400 at +50%); dial the slider down as pops grow.
check: Confirm your Energy balance, district specialization slots, and automation slider in the colony UI before enabling.

sources: GamerOfPassion 4.6 Dangerous Technology Guide (verified against 4.6.0 game files)
steps: Red (Dangerous) technologies do not pick which Endgame Crisis spawns—Jump Drives only move the first crisis roll earlier from 2450 to 2425.
To avoid a Machine Uprising when researching Synthetics/Sapient AI, grant AI Citizen Rights (or outlaw robots) before ~2290.
Keep a non-Sapient Combat Computer backup ship design in case the Contingency spawns, and avoid the Restrictions Imposed policy unless needed because it applies a -20% rare tech draw penalty.
check: Verify your Artificial Intelligence policy, Research Restrictions policy, and ship computer designs in game.

sources: GamerOfPassion 4.6 Ascension Perks Guide (verified against 4.6.0 game files)
steps: Reserve an open Tradition tree slot before adopting your 7th Tradition so you have room for your chosen Ascension Path tree.
Strong early no-DLC openings include Technological Ascendancy, Transcendent Learning, and Imperial Prerogative (-25% Empire Size from colonies).
For late-game security or 4.6 builds, consider Defender of the Galaxy (+50% crisis damage), Galactic Force Projection (+150 naval cap), or 4.6 Willpower's Force of Will ambition.
check: Confirm perk prerequisites, open Tradition slots, and DLC/ethics eligibility in the Traditions & Relics screen.
